Rashi on Zevachim 16a:1:1.english: A zar [non-priest], who does not eat - [this refers to eating] of the most holy offerings.

Rashi on Zevachim 16a:2:1.english: For it made the offered [animal] like the one offering [it] - A blemish disqualifies in an offering the same way it disqualifies in a priest.

Rashi on Zevachim 16a:3:1.hebrew: טמא יוכיח - שלא עשה בו קרב כמקריב, שאין בהמה מקבלת טומאה מחיים כשם שהכהן טמא מחיים, וכתיב וינזרו ולא יחללו, אלמא טמא שעבד חילל:
Rashi on Zevachim 16a:3:1.english: The impure [priest] shall prove [it] - [Unlike a blemished priest,] with an impure priest he did not make the offering equivalent to the offerer, since an animal does not contract impurity while alive, whereas the priest can be impure while alive. Yet it is written, "that they separate themselves... and not profane" (Leviticus 22:2) - proving that an impure priest who performed the service has profaned [the offering].

Rashi on Zevachim 16a:4:1.english: That they are warned: that a tamei person may not serve is derived from [the verse] "veyinnazru" (Leviticus 22:2), and that a blemished priest [may not serve is derived] from "velo yigash" (Leviticus 21:21).

Tosafot on Zevachim 16a:1:1.hebrew: זר שאינו אוכל כו' - ואין לומר: דטמא בקרבן צבור וכהן גדול אונן יוכיח, שאינן אוכלין ועובדים. דמה להנך שכן אינן מוזהרים, תאמר בזר דמוזהר:
Tosafot on Zevachim 16a:1:1.english: A zar, who does not eat, etc. - And one cannot say: let the tamei [priest, in the case of] a communal offering, and a Kohen Gadol who is an onen, prove it - for they do not eat [from the offering], yet they [still] perform the service. [The reason this proof fails is:] what comparison is there to these? For they are not warned [i.e., not subject to a prohibition against serving in that state] - would you say the same of a zar, who is warned?

Tosafot on Zevachim 16a:3:1.english: What is [notable] about an impure priest? That he imparts impurity - One cannot raise the objection, "since [Scripture] made the offering[s] equivalent to the offerer[s]" [as was raised regarding a blemished priest], as explained in the Kuntres [i.e., Rashi's commentary].
